Respiratory system.question: ১) Where gaseous exchange doesn't take place?
Respiratory system.exp:
Gaseous exchange occurs across the respiratory portion of the respiratory tract, where alveoli are present.

  • Terminal bronchiole → conducts air only; no gas exchange

  • Respiratory bronchiole → gas exchange begins

  • Alveolar duct → gas exchange occurs

  • Alveoli → main site of gas exchange

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Conducting zone: nose → terminal bronchioles → no gas exchange

  • Respiratory zone: respiratory bronchioles → alveolar ducts → alveoli → gas exchange

Exam Pearl:
Gas exchange does NOT occur in the terminal bronchiole.

Respiratory system.question: ২) Which is not one of the five cell types of respiratory epithelium?
Respiratory system.exp:
The five major cell types of respiratory epithelium are classically:

  1. Ciliated columnar cells

  2. Goblet cells

  3. Basal cells

  4. Brush cells

  5. Small granular (neuroendocrine/Kulchitsky) cells

Therefore, large granular cell is not one of the five typical cell types.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ciliated columnar → mucociliary clearance

  • Goblet → mucus secretion

  • Basal → stem/progenitor cells

  • Brush → sensory function

  • Small granular → neuroendocrine cells

Exam Pearl:
Respiratory epithelium has small granular cells, not large granular cells.

Respiratory system.question: ৩) Bronchopulmonary segment is constituted by......?
Respiratory system.exp:
A bronchopulmonary segment is a structurally and functionally independent subdivision of a lung lobe supplied by a segmental (tertiary) bronchus and a corresponding branch of the pulmonary artery.

  • Primary bronchus → supplies an entire lung.

  • Secondary/lobar bronchus → supplies a lung lobe.

  • Tertiary/segmental bronchus → supplies a bronchopulmonary segment.

  • Lobar bronchus → same as secondary bronchus.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Primary bronchus → lung

  • Secondary bronchus → lobe

  • Tertiary bronchus → bronchopulmonary segment

  • Each segment → pyramidal, surgically resectable unit.

Exam Pearl:
Bronchopulmonary segment = territory supplied by a tertiary (segmental) bronchus.

Respiratory system.question: ৪) What type of cartilage is present in trachea?
Respiratory system.exp:
The trachea contains C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage. These rings provide structural support and prevent collapse of the airway during breathing. The posterior gap in the cartilage rings is bridged by the trachealis muscle.

  • Hyaline cartilage → trachea and bronchi

  • Elastic cartilage → epiglottis, pinna

  • Fibrocartilage → intervertebral discs, pubic symphysis

  • No cartilage → bronchioles

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Trachea → C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings

  • Bronchi → cartilage plates

  • Bronchioles → no cartilage

  • Epiglottis → elastic cartilage

Exam Pearl:
Trachea = hyaline cartilage.

Respiratory system.question: ৫) Which is responsible for spongy structure of lung?
Respiratory system.exp:
The spongy appearance and texture of the lungs are mainly due to the enormous number of alveoli, which are tiny air-filled sacs surrounded by pulmonary capillaries. They occupy most of the functional lung tissue and provide the large surface area required for gas exchange.

  • Bronchi → conduct air but do not create the characteristic spongy texture.

  • Bronchioles → small conducting/respiratory airways.

  • Alveoli → responsible for the spongy structure of the lung.

  • Alveolar ducts → passages leading to alveolar sacs.

Exam Pearl:
Spongy structure of lung → alveoli.

Respiratory system.question: ৬) Which is not true about right lung?
Respiratory system.exp:
The right lung has 3 lobes (upper, middle, lower) separated by 2 fissures (oblique and horizontal). It does not have a cardiac notch; the prominent cardiac notch is a feature of the left lung. The lingula is also absent in the right lung.

  • 3 lobes → True

  • 2 fissures → True

  • Cardiac notch present → False

  • Lingula absent → True

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Right lung: 3 lobes + 2 fissures + no cardiac notch/lingula

  • Left lung: 2 lobes + 1 fissure + cardiac notch + lingula

Exam Pearl:
Cardiac notch and lingula → left lung.

Respiratory system.question: ৭) Which is the chief component of lung surfactant?
Respiratory system.exp:
The chief component of pulmonary surfactant is dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC), also called lecithin. It is produced by type II pneumocytes and reduces alveolar surface tension, helping prevent alveolar collapse (atelectasis), particularly during expiration.

  • DPPC → major/chief surfactant phospholipid

  • Phosphatidylglycerol → important minor phospholipid

  • Neutral lipids → present in smaller amounts

  • Proteins → surfactant proteins (SP-A, SP-B, SP-C, SP-D), but not the chief component

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Surfactant source → Type II pneumocytes

  • Chief component → DPPC (lecithin)

  • Main function → ↓ surface tension

  • Deficiency → neonatal respiratory distress syndrome

Exam Pearl:
Pulmonary surfactant = mainly DPPC (lecithin).

Respiratory system.question: ৮) What is the value of inspiratory reserve volume?
Respiratory system.exp:
Inspiratory reserve volume (IRV) is the additional volume of air that can be forcefully inspired after a normal tidal inspiration.

The standard approximate value in an average adult is 3000 mL (3 L).

  • Tidal volume (TV) → 500 mL

  • Inspiratory reserve volume (IRV) → 3000 mL

  • Expiratory reserve volume (ERV) → 1100 mL

  • Residual volume (RV) → 1200 mL

High-Yield Rapid Recall:
TV 500 + IRV 3000 + ERV 1100 + RV 1200 mL

Exam Pearl:
IRV = ~3000 mL.

Respiratory system.question: ৯) The volume of air remaining in the lung after normal expiration is called.......?
Respiratory system.exp:
Functional residual capacity (FRC) is the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a normal, quiet expiration.

FRC = ERV + RV

  • Inspiratory capacity (IC) = TV + IRV

  • Vital capacity (VC) = IRV + TV + ERV

  • FRC = ERV + RV ✅

  • Total lung capacity (TLC) = VC + RV

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • After normal expiration → FRC

  • After maximum expiration → RV

  • After maximum inspiration → TLC

Exam Pearl:
Air remaining after normal expiration = FRC.

Respiratory system.question: ১০) Which factor dissociates oxygen hemoglobin dissociation curve to the right?
Respiratory system.exp:
A rightward shift of the oxygen–hemoglobin dissociation curve means reduced hemoglobin affinity for O₂, facilitating oxygen unloading to tissues.

A decrease in pH causes a rightward shift via the Bohr effect.

  • ↓ pH → right shift ✅

  • ↓ body temperature → left shift

  • ↓ 2,3-BPG → left shift

  • ↓ PCO₂ → left shift

High-Yield Rapid Recall — Right Shift (“CADET, face Right”):

  • C → CO₂ ↑

  • A → Acidity (H⁺) ↑ / pH ↓

  • D → 2,3-DPG ↑

  • E → Exercise

  • T → Temperature ↑

Exam Pearl:
↓ pH → right shift → easier O₂ unloading to tissues.

Respiratory system.question: ১১) Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is useful in all except.........?
Respiratory system.exp:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) is used for several specific conditions involving tissue hypoxia or gas bubbles.

  • Gas gangrene → established indication; improves tissue oxygenation and helps control Clostridium infection.

  • CO poisoning → HBOT can accelerate elimination of carbon monoxide from hemoglobin.

  • Nitrogen toxicity/decompression sickness → treated with recompression and hyperbaric oxygen.

  • Congenital heart disease → not a standard indication for HBOT. ✅

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HBOT → CO poisoning

  • HBOT → Gas gangrene

  • HBOT → Decompression sickness

  • HBOT → selected ischemic/wound conditions

Exam Pearl:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is NOT routinely used for congenital heart disease.

Respiratory system.question: ১২) The point at which breathing cannot longer be voluntarily inhibited is called......?
Respiratory system.exp:
The breaking point is the point during voluntary breath-holding at which the urge to breathe becomes so strong that breathing can no longer be voluntarily inhibited.

The main stimulus is rising PaCO₂ and H⁺ concentration, which strongly stimulates the respiratory centres.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Voluntary breath-holding → PaCO₂ gradually rises

  • Strong respiratory drive develops → urge to breathe

  • Point where voluntary inhibition fails → Breaking point

Exam Pearl:
Cannot voluntarily hold breath any longer = Breaking point.

Respiratory system.question: ১৩) Which is not a criteria of small cell carcinoma of lung?
Respiratory system.exp:
Small cell carcinoma of the lung (SCLC) is strongly associated with smoking, is more common in men, and is one of the most aggressive/high-grade lung cancers. It is also strongly associated with paraneoplastic syndromes because of its neuroendocrine origin.

Common paraneoplastic syndromes include:

  • SIADH → ectopic ADH secretion

  • Cushing syndrome → ectopic ACTH secretion

  • Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome

Therefore, “paraneoplastic syndrome absent” is false.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • SCLC → smoker + central/hilar tumor

  • Very aggressive, early metastasis

  • Strongly associated with paraneoplastic syndromes

  • SIADH, ectopic ACTH, Lambert-Eaton

Exam Pearl:
Small cell carcinoma + paraneoplastic syndromes = classic association.

Respiratory system.question: ১৪) Langhan's giant cells are present in........?
Respiratory system.exp:
Langhans giant cells are multinucleated giant cells formed by the fusion of activated macrophages and are classically found in granulomatous inflammation, especially tuberculosis.

In TB, the typical granuloma contains:

  • Caseous necrosis centrally

  • Epithelioid cells

  • Langhans giant cells

  • Surrounding lymphocytes

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Condition Typical finding
TB Caseating granuloma + Langhans giant cells
Bronchogenic carcinoma Malignant epithelial cells
CAP Acute inflammatory infiltrate
ILD Interstitial fibrosis/inflammation

Exam Pearl:
Langhans giant cells → think TB.

Respiratory system.question: ১৫) Features of bronchopneumonia excludes......?
Respiratory system.exp:
Bronchopneumonia is characterized by patchy, multifocal consolidation centered around bronchioles and often involving multiple lobes, frequently in dependent areas.

  • Patchy consolidation → characteristic

  • No definite organism → can be true clinically because many organisms can cause bronchopneumonia

  • Extremes of age → commonly affected

  • Only single lobe affected → not typical; this describes lobar pneumonia more closely

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bronchopneumonia → patchy, multilobar, bronchiolar distribution

  • Lobar pneumonia → consolidation of a large portion/all of one lobe

  • Bronchopneumonia → common at extremes of age

Exam Pearl:
Patchy + multilobar consolidation = bronchopneumonia; single-lobe consolidation = lobar pneumonia.

Respiratory system.question: ১৬) In lobar pneumonia what is the duration of stage of grey hepatisation?
Respiratory system.exp:
In classical lobar pneumonia, grey hepatization is the third stage and typically occurs around day 4–8.

The classical stages are:

  1. Congestion → 1st day

  2. Red hepatization → 2nd–3rd day

  3. Grey hepatization → 4th–8th day ✅

  4. Resolution → from about 8th day onward

During grey hepatization, RBCs disintegrate, while fibrin and leukocytes remain, giving the lung a grey, firm, liver-like appearance.

Exam Pearl:
Lobar pneumonia: Red hepatization = 2–3 days → Grey hepatization = 4–8 days.

Respiratory system.question: ১৭) What type of emphysema predominantly occurs in heavy smoker?
Respiratory system.exp:
Centriacinar emphysema is strongly associated with cigarette smoking and predominantly affects the upper lobes, especially the upper zones of the lungs. It initially involves the respiratory bronchioles, while the distal alveoli are relatively spared.

  • Centriacinar → smoking, upper lobes ✅

  • Panacinar → classically α₁-antitrypsin deficiency, lower lobes

  • Distal acinar (paraseptal) → associated with bullae and spontaneous pneumothorax

  • Irregular → associated with scarring

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Type Classic association
Centriacinar Smoking
Panacinar α₁-antitrypsin deficiency
Paraseptal Spontaneous pneumothorax
Irregular Pulmonary fibrosis/scarring

Exam Pearl:
Heavy smoker → centriacinar emphysema.

Respiratory system.question: ১৮) Episodic wheezing, cough & dyspnea are featured in.......?
Respiratory system.exp:
Asthma classically presents with episodic (paroxysmal) wheezing, cough, and dyspnea due to reversible airway obstruction caused by bronchial hyperresponsiveness, airway inflammation, and bronchoconstriction.

  • Asthma → episodic/recurrent wheeze + cough + dyspnea ✅

  • Chronic bronchitis → chronic productive cough for ≥3 months in 2 consecutive years

  • Bronchiectasis → chronic productive cough with copious purulent sputum

  • Emphysema → progressive dyspnea, typically with less prominent cough

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Asthma → variable + reversible airflow obstruction

  • Wheeze → bronchoconstriction

  • Common triggers → allergens, exercise, cold air, infections

Exam Pearl:
Episodic wheezing + cough + dyspnea = Asthma.

Respiratory system.question: ১৯) Which is cause of bilateral pleural effusion?
Respiratory system.exp:
Congestive cardiac failure (CCF) is a common cause of bilateral pleural effusion, usually due to increased hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary circulation. The resulting effusion is typically a transudate.

  • CCF → commonly bilateral pleural effusion ✅

  • Pneumonia → usually unilateral parapneumonic effusion

  • TB → usually unilateral exudative effusion

  • Bronchial carcinoma → generally unilateral, often malignant exudative effusion

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bilateral pleural effusion → think CCF

  • CCF → transudate

  • TB/malignancy/pneumonia → usually exudate

Exam Pearl:
Common bilateral pleural effusion = CCF.

Respiratory system.question: ২০) Which is not true about pleural fluid study finding in pneumonia?
Respiratory system.exp:
In parapneumonic pleural effusion, the fluid is typically exudative, turbid, and neutrophil-predominant due to acute bacterial inflammation.

Increased ADA (adenosine deaminase) is classically associated with tuberculous pleural effusion, where the fluid is usually lymphocyte-predominant.

  • Turbid → True

  • ADA increased → Not typically true in pneumonia ✅

  • Exudative → True

  • Neutrophil predominant → True

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bacterial/parapneumonic effusion → exudate + neutrophils

  • TB pleural effusion → exudate + lymphocytes + ↑ ADA

  • Empyema → pus, very low pH/glucose, high LDH

Exam Pearl:
↑ ADA → think TB, not uncomplicated bacterial pneumonia.

Respiratory system.question: ২১) How is the percussion note in pneumothorax?
Respiratory system.exp:
In pneumothorax, air accumulates in the pleural cavity. This increased amount of air produces a hyper-resonant percussion note over the affected area.

  • Hyper-resonant → pneumothorax ✅

  • Resonant → normal lung

  • Woody dull → classically associated with consolidation

  • Stony dull → pleural effusion

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Condition Percussion note
Normal lung Resonant
Pneumothorax Hyper-resonant
Consolidation Dull
Pleural effusion Stony dull

Exam Pearl:
Pneumothorax → hyper-resonant percussion note.

Respiratory system.question: ২২) In which step of management of bronchial asthma LABA is added?
Respiratory system.exp:
In the traditional stepwise management of bronchial asthma, a long-acting β₂-agonist (LABA) is added at Step 3, usually in combination with an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS).

  • Step 1 → reliever therapy

  • Step 2 → low-dose ICS

  • Step 3 → low-dose ICS + LABA ✅

  • Step 4 → higher-dose ICS + LABA

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Step Typical therapy
Step 1 Reliever
Step 2 Low-dose ICS
Step 3 ICS + LABA
Step 4 Higher-dose ICS + LABA

Exam Pearl:
Asthma → LABA is classically added at Step 3.

Respiratory system.question: ২৩) Which is not true about inspection finding of COPD?
Respiratory system.exp:
The respiratory rate in COPD is generally normal or increased, especially during respiratory distress. Therefore, decreased respiratory rate is not a typical inspection finding.

  • Barrel-shaped chest → common in advanced emphysema

  • Decreased respiratory rate → not typical ✅

  • Pursed-lip breathing → characteristic of COPD, especially emphysema

  • Intercostal recession → may occur due to increased work of breathing

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • COPD → barrel chest

  • Pursed-lip breathing → prolonged expiration

  • Increased work of breathing → accessory muscle use/recession

  • Severe COPD → tachypnea, not typically bradypnea

Exam Pearl:
COPD inspection: barrel chest + pursed lips + increased work of breathing; decreased RR is not typical.

Respiratory system.question: ২৪) Which investigation is done to confirm emphysema?
Respiratory system.exp:
High-resolution CT (HRCT) of the chest is the most sensitive imaging investigation for demonstrating the structural changes of emphysema, such as low-attenuation areas, bullae, and destruction of alveolar walls.

  • CXR → may suggest emphysema (hyperinflation, flattened diaphragm) but is less sensitive.

  • CT → can detect emphysematous changes.

  • HRCT → best for detailed assessment of emphysema ✅

  • MRI → not routinely used to diagnose emphysema.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Emphysema → HRCT for structural assessment

  • CXR → hyperinflation, flattened diaphragm

  • Spirometry → confirms airflow obstruction (↓FEV₁/FVC)

Exam Pearl:
Best imaging investigation for emphysema = HRCT chest.

Respiratory system.question: ২৫) CURB-65 scoring system is done to assess severity of which disease?
Respiratory system.exp:
CURB-65 is a clinical scoring system used to assess the severity of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and help determine the need for hospital admission.

CURB-65:

  • C → Confusion

  • U → Urea > 7 mmol/L

  • R → Respiratory rate ≥ 30/min

  • B → Blood pressure: systolic <90 or diastolic ≤60 mmHg

  • 65 → Age ≥65 years

Each criterion scores 1 point.

Exam Pearl:
CURB-65 → severity assessment of community-acquired pneumonia.
